# Results — Study 109 (OBV-Divergence) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Two signals tested:
(A) OBV trend vs its 20-day SMA as a directional signal; (B) OBV-vs-price divergence
as a reversal predictor. Both run on six liquid names (SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA),
daily bars, 5-day forward return horizon, vs an unconditional baseline and a random-entry
control. As-of **2026-06-13**.*

## Unconditional baseline

The buy-and-hold 5-day forward return on SPY (the non-signal benchmark):

| n | mean (bps/5d) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 4,130 | **+22.88** | **+3.65** |

This is the unconditional equity risk premium leaking through the 5-day window.
Both OBV signals must beat *this* bar to claim a timing edge — neither does.

## Signal A: OBV trend / cross (OBV vs SMA(OBV, 20)) — gross, 5-day horizon

| Ticker | n | win-rate | mean (bps/signal) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 4,111 | 52.2% | −3.34 | −0.62 |
| QQQ  | 4,111 | 53.2% | +5.48 | +0.85 |
| IWM  | 4,111 | 48.9% | −6.88 | −0.88 |
| AAPL | 4,111 | 52.6% | +8.74 | +0.86 |
| MSFT | 4,111 | 49.9% | −14.10 | −1.73 |
| NVDA | 4,111 | 49.9% | −1.13 | −0.07 |
| **Pooled** | **24,666** | **51.1%** | **−1.87** | **−0.47** |
| Random control | 24,666 | 50.0% | −4.36 | −1.83 |

- Pooled gross expectancy is **−1.87 bps/signal**, HAC t = **−0.47** — statistically
  indistinguishable from zero.
- Signal A does **not beat the random-direction control** on any consistent basis;
  the Δ vs coin is only **+2.49 bps** in the pooled data and no individual ticker
  clears |t| ≥ 2.
- The OBV trend direction adds nothing beyond a coin flip: every per-instrument |t| < 1.8.

## Signal B: OBV-price divergence reversal (lookback=10d, OBV SMA=5d) — gross, 5d horizon

| Ticker | n signals | win-rate | mean (bps/signal) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 903 | 46.6% | −15.57 | −1.58 |
| QQQ  | 884 | 50.5% | −2.77 | −0.22 |
| IWM  | 942 | 46.9% | −17.64 | −1.40 |
| AAPL | 895 | 48.8% | −8.92 | −0.53 |
| MSFT | 1,008 | 50.9% | +3.32 | +0.22 |
| NVDA | 896 | 47.3% | −18.32 | −0.73 |
| **Pooled** | **5,528** | **48.5%** | **−9.80** | **−1.48** |
| Random control | 5,528 | 49.5% | −4.92 | −1.09 |

- Divergence signals are **worse** than the random-direction control by **−4.88 bps**,
  and the pooled gross is **−9.80 bps/signal**, HAC t = **−1.48** (sub-threshold).
- Far from predicting reversals, the OBV divergence signal fires with a slight *bearish*
  bias (the winning unconditional drift means fighting the trend is costly). No instrument
  shows a reversal edge that clears the inference bar.

## Cost sweep — Signal A

Every signal costs approximately 1 trade/day; a realistic round-trip ranges from 1–5 bps.

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/signal) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −1.87 | −0.47 |
| 1.0 bps | −2.87 | −0.72 |
| 2.0 bps | −3.87 | −0.96 |
| 5.0 bps | −6.87 | −1.71 |

Even at zero cost Signal A is a slight loser. At any realistic transaction cost
it is a statistically significant underperformer vs the passive alternative.

## Multiple-comparison note

Two signals × six instruments = 12 tests. Under the Bonferroni correction for 12
independent tests the threshold for the family-wise error rate α=0.05 is |t| ≥ 3.0.
Not a single test clears even the uncorrected |t| ≥ 2.0, so multiple-comparison
adjustment is moot — there is nothing to inflate.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Signal A gross HAC t = −0.47; Signal B gross HAC t = −1.48.
  Neither clears the |t| ≥ 2 inference bar on any instrument or in the pool.
  The divergence signal is also sub-random (loses to a coin flip by −4.88 bps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Both signals start negative gross; any transaction cost
  makes them significant losers vs buy-and-hold. Signal A underperforms the passive
  5-day drift by +24.75 bps/signal (unconditional: +22.88 bps, signal: −1.87 bps).
- **Volume precedes price? — NOT SUPPORTED.** OBV neither times the market (Signal A)
  nor predicts reversals (Signal B) at a statistically credible level. Volume confirms
  rather than leads price in this 16-year daily dataset.
